### 🟡 Changes recommended The comparator can incorrectly accept differing row multiplicities when canonicalized rows and raw counts match. *Once you've addressed the issues Copilot identified, you can request another Copilot review.*
Pull request overview This pull request repairs UPDATE differential-test adjudication while preserving Sparq-only regression coverage. **Changes:** - Separates canonical and noncanonical integer pools. - Strengthens lexical, row, blank-node, and structural checks. - Adds generator, nested-term, LOAD, and historical regression tests.

The new row-preservation checks are bypassed when blank-node canonicalization makes `ca == cb`: `comparable` deduplicates canonical lines, and this branch only compares total raw lengths. Thus a dataset with `[p, p, q]` versus `[p, q, q]` has equal canonical sets and equal raw counts and returns `Same`; the `subject == "_:x"` case in `lexical_adjudication_preserves_rows_and_blank_node_structure` exercises exactly this path and will not return `Differs`. Compare multiplicities (or run the normalized snapshot checks) before the early `ca == cb` return, rather than relying on total row counts.
